# upwind_threat_story (Data Source)

Reads a single Upwind threat story by ID. Stories are generated by the platform and cannot be managed as a resource.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A single story by id. This is the only endpoint that returns `description`
# and `status_reason`; the collection endpoints omit them.
#
# A story id that does not exist is an error, not an empty result: a data
# source has no state to drop, so a missing object fails the plan.
data "upwind_threat_story" "incident" {
  id = "sty-1a2b3c4d5e6f7890"
}

output "incident_summary" {
  value = {
    title    = data.upwind_threat_story.incident.title
    severity = data.upwind_threat_story.incident.severity
    status   = data.upwind_threat_story.incident.status
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `id` (String) Unique identifier of the story to read.

### Read-Only

- `create_time` (String) ISO8601 timestamp when the story was created.
- `description` (String) Detailed description of the story. Returned only by this single-story lookup, not by `upwind_threat_stories`.
- `detection_ids` (List of String) IDs of the detections that make up this story.
- `severity` (String) Severity: `CRITICAL`, `HIGH`, `MEDIUM`, `LOW`, or `INFO`. Note the uppercase, which differs from the lowercase severities used by threat policies.
- `status` (String) Status: `OPEN` or `ARCHIVED`.
- `status_reason` (String) Reason the story was archived. Null if the story is open or was archived without a reason.
- `title` (String) Story title.
- `update_time` (String) ISO8601 timestamp when the story was last updated.
